title: Kenyan Sweet Cassava Chips
community: Popular along the coast and increasingly nationwide
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Sweet Cassava Chips — thin cassava slices boiled briefly then deep-fried until golden and crispy, tossed in cinnamon sugar while hot. A sweet-savoury Kenyan snack with a naturally creamy interior and wonderfully crunchy exterior.
longDesc: Sweet cassava chips take the cassava chip concept in a dessert direction — the cinnamon sugar coating applied while the chips are hot creates a lightly caramelised, fragrant surface that makes them completely addictive. They sit happily between snack and dessert, equally at home with tea or as an after-school treat.
steps: Peel cassava, remove the woody central fibre, and slice into thin rounds (3—4mm).
Pre-boil the cassava slices in salted water for 8—10 minutes until just partially tender. Drain and dry thoroughly.
Mix sugar, cinnamon, salt, and nutmeg in a bowl. Set aside.
Fry cassava slices in batches for 3—4 minutes until golden and crispy.
While still hot, toss in the cinnamon sugar mixture.
chefTips: Pre-boiling is essential for cassava chips — raw cassava will not cook through in frying time.
Dry thoroughly after boiling — wet cassava spatters dangerously in hot oil.
Season immediately while hot — the sugar adheres and lightly caramelises on the warm surface.
commonMistakes: Wet cassava in the fryer — dangerous splatter.
Not seasoning while hot — the cinnamon sugar does not adhere.
cookingScience: Pre-boiling gelatinises the cassava starch, creating the characteristically creamy interior. The subsequent frying dehydrates the exterior and creates the crunchy shell through Maillard browning.
sustainabilityTips: Cassava is a drought-resistant, sustainable crop.
storage: Best eaten immediately — loses crispiness within an hour.
culturalNote: Sweet cassava chips are a beloved coastal and increasingly national snack that showcases the versatility of cassava — Kenya's most underrated root vegetable.
